Subject: Operational assurance addendum & evidence flow for Private Deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Clintegrity’s infra team is greenlighting a move to a private deployment for our clinical inference pipelines, and procurement/legal asked me to start a focused thread on the addendum language and evidence flow we’ll need in the MSA/Order Form. High level asks from our side: 

- Clear license scope for on‑prem instance (what the customer can snapshot/retain, and what counts as retained IP)
- Operator access boundary (temporary read‑only validation windows vs. ongoing operator console access)
- Snapshot transfer & custody evidence (we prefer an "escrow‑lite" approach: sealed snapshot + attestations + on‑site witness if needed)
- Audit evidence package (what artifacts you can provide: logs, attestation, signed manifests)

Can you circulate a proposed Exhibit (we call it Exhibit: Operational Assurance) and an outline of the evidence binder Clintegrity would receive during go‑live and at acceptance? Procurement would like to know a realistic timeline for redlines and any tech prerequisites from your product team.

Appreciate it — would like to have legal look at a draft by the end of next week if possible.

Best,
Susan Park
Director, Cloud Architecture
Clintegrity Health

Susan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first pass: "operational-assurance-exhibit-draft_v1.docx" (Exhibit D) and a short evidence binder outline. High‑level notes up front: 

- License scope: draft language differentiates model binary residency vs. customer data; includes an explicit carve for customer snapshots created from their input data.
- Operator access: draft favors a sealed‑snapshot + time‑boxed remote validation window (NDA + witness) rather than persistent console operator access — this aligns with a lot of regulated customers and reduces ongoing blast radius.
- Snapshot custody: proposed a signed manifest + SHA256 hash of the snapshot, notarized by the witnessing engineer, plus a one‑time transfer procedure.
- Audit artifacts: we list specific logs, runbooks, and an attestation template that we can populate during evidence delivery.

Timeline: we can get a redline of Exhibit D for your legal by 48 business hours if you confirm the high‑level approach above. If Clintegrity requires a live, read‑only validation window instead of sealed snapshot-only validation, we should lock that expectation now because it affects operator tooling and scheduling.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm whether sealed snapshot + short live validation window is acceptable.
2) Clintegrity legal provides target redline deadline and any mandatory wording.
3) We circulate a tracked Exhibit D and the evidence binder outline.

I’ll also loop in Product and Legal internally to confirm feasibility of the attachment/attestation flow.

Specific product/legal clarifications we need:

- Attestation witness: does Legal/Compliance require a specific witness script or only a signed, dated witness statement?

I’ve attached an "evidence-binder-outline.docx". If Legal can redline Exhibit D within 48 business hours I’ll send the tracked version to Clintegrity. Please flag any non‑negotiable constraints — procurement is eager to lock timing.

Karthik / Susan — Mike Long on behalf of Clintegrity Legal. Thanks for circulating the draft. A few points from procurement/legal after an initial review: 

- Operator access: Clintegrity cannot approve persistent operator console access. We are open to a sealed snapshot + notarized manifest approach plus a single short, time‑boxed read‑only validation window under NDA. That window should be limited (we propose 60 minutes) and require an auditable session log.
- Snapshot custody & proof: we require a signed manifest with per‑file SHA256 hashes and a witness attestation (signed by the Redwood engineer and a Clintegrity witness) at handover. If Redwood can provide an HSM‑backed signature on the manifest, that is preferred; otherwise a notarized attestation is acceptable.
- Indemnity/derivative rights: please confirm that snapshot transfer does not grant Redwood ownership of derived models trained on Clintegrity data — we want an explicit carve that customer‑derived models remain customer IP.
- Audit artifacts: please confirm the retention window for logs included in the evidence binder and whether they will include any PII/PHI (we expect sanitized exports only).

Attached is our "Clintegrity-Attestation-Reqs.pdf" with a procurement timeline and a short template for the witness attestation. We’re targeting a 2‑week review cycle on the Exhibit if Redwood can respond to the items above and produce the redline + a short feasibility note re: HSM signature.

Regards,
Mike Long

Clintegrity Health
